Spastic paraplegia with peripheral neuropathy; amyotrophy is neurogenic. Urinary urgency alone does not establish urinary tract damage; hearing loss occurs in 20%.
Demyelinating neuropathy and early glaucoma define the subtype. Structural foot/spinal deformities and vocal cord paralysis each occur in 30-79%; hearing loss is under 30%.
Nonbacterial erosion damages dental pulp; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Mixed central and peripheral nerve tumours with cutaneous neurofibromas define this historical phenotype; Lisch nodules do not establish damaging ocular involvement.
Inherited neurodegenerative movement disorder with common cognitive impairment, chorea, rigidity and ataxia.
Defined by developmental abnormalities of individual bones or groups of bones; additional organ findings vary across subtypes.
Pregnancy-associated chorea is a neurologic movement disorder; associated rheumatic or collagen vascular diseases do not establish an immune mechanism in every case.
Defined by gastric and intestinal dysfunction after gastrectomy; hypoglycemia and nutritional deficiencies are variable manifestations across this umbrella.
T-cell immunodeficiency, deficient sweat glands/hair and abnormal or missing teeth define the syndrome. Recurrent infections and organ enlargement alone add no damaged organ.
Congenital structural abnormality of the mitral valve's subvalvular apparatus.
Isolated adhesion of the labia minora affects reproductive anatomy; no urinary tract damage is established.
Poikiloderma, cataracts and skeletal dysplasia define the phenotype. GH deficiency occurs in 6/6 and hypothyroidism in 5/6; developmental delay is below 30%.
Renal tubular developmental failure defines the disease; drug causation does not change its affected organ.
Mucinous dilation involves the exocrine pancreatic ducts; endocrine pancreatic involvement is not established.
Benign tumour arising in mammary ducts; breast tissue lies outside the specified axes.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Fluid accumulation in lung tissue impairs gas exchange. Heart failure is a possible underlying cause, not an organ damaged by pulmonary edema.
Neurodevelopmental impairment is a common manifestation of pathogenic partial X duplications; other organ abnormalities depend on the duplicated segment and sex.
Tumour arises in the uterine round ligament, a reproductive support structure rather than a ligament of the locomotor system.
Defined by Toxascaris nematode infection; the supplied concept does not establish common damage to a particular organ.
Lipomatous adipose overgrowth; bladder/ureter compression causes obstructive urinary tract damage in roughly 30-50%. Constipation alone does not establish bowel damage.
Familial cerebral neurodegeneration with amyloid, neurofibrillary tangles and spongiform pathology; prion pathology alone does not establish an infection.
Defined by deficient ossification of the parietal bones. Vascular and brain abnormalities occur below 30%; intellectual disability and seizures are very rare.
